blocks.text: 1. AlexNet

blocks.alt: AlexNet chains five conv layers and three fully connected layers to a 1000 class output

blocks.text: LeNet, the previous topic, proved the core Convolutional Neural Network concept at a genuinely small scale decades earlier. AlexNet is the architecture that helped launch the modern deep learning era, explored throughout this topic.
It is a genuinely much deeper, larger network trained on genuinely large-scale image data, a genuinely dramatic leap forward from LeNet's own small scale already covered in the previous topic.
2. The Scale Leap

blocks.alt: LeNet was small scale while AlexNet went much deeper

blocks.text: This connects back to a parameter count perspective, already covered in LeNet. AlexNet is genuinely dramatically larger than LeNet, with far more layers and parameters, already covered there as a useful baseline for comparison.
This is a genuinely direct answer to the scale limitation already covered in the previous topic, demonstrating exactly how much larger a genuinely practical, modern network could become.
3. GPU Enablement

blocks.alt: CPU training is compared against GPU training

blocks.text: A genuinely important, real enabling factor connects back to Mixed Precision Training's own hardware theme, already covered in the Training Deep Networks module. AlexNet's own genuinely large scale only became genuinely practical thanks to Graphics Processing Unit training.
This genuinely direct dependence on specialized hardware, already covered generally in that earlier topic, was a genuinely important practical enabler that made AlexNet's own scale achievable at all.

blocks.text: 4. The ReLU Breakthrough

blocks.alt: Sigmoid activation is slow while ReLU is fast

blocks.text: This connects back to ReLU, already covered in the Activation Functions module. AlexNet genuinely popularized ReLU over the older Sigmoid and Tanh activations, already covered there.
This directly helped address the vanishing gradient problem, already covered throughout Activation Functions, a genuinely important practical contribution beyond AlexNet's own specific architecture.
5. Popularizing Dropout

blocks.alt: Dropout randomly disables units during training to reduce overfitting

blocks.text: This connects back to Dropout, already covered in the Regularization Techniques module. AlexNet genuinely helped popularize Dropout as a practical, effective regularization technique, demonstrating its genuine, real-world value at scale.

This is a genuinely important, real historical contribution beyond just its own architecture, since Dropout's own later widespread adoption, already covered in its own topic, owes much to this genuinely successful early demonstration.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: AlexNet's own genuinely successful combination of ReLU and Dropout, both already covered in this topic, is a genuinely important historical reason both techniques became such widely adopted, standard defaults in later deep learning practice.

blocks.text: 6. The Overall Structure

This connects back to LeNet's own overall structure, already covered in the previous topic. AlexNet follows a genuinely similar convolution-then-fully-connected pattern, just at genuinely much larger scale.

This confirms that the core pattern already covered in LeNet genuinely still applies, just scaled up dramatically, exactly the kind of continuity that connects these two historically significant architectures together.
7. The Choice Of Larger Early Filters

blocks.alt: A large first filter gives a wide early receptive field

blocks.text: This connects back to filter size, already covered in Filters and Kernels. AlexNet's genuinely earliest layers use somewhat larger filters than LeNet's own genuinely small ones, already covered in that earlier topic.

This is a design choice later architectures, covered further in this module, would genuinely reconsider, favoring smaller filters stacked more deeply instead, a genuinely important theme explored in the next several topics of this module.
8. A Genuine Competition Milestone

blocks.alt: AlexNet won ImageNet 2012 and halved the error rate

blocks.text: A genuinely important historical milestone connects back to Evaluation Metrics, already covered in its own module. AlexNet genuinely won a major, high-profile image classification competition by a genuinely dramatic margin.

This genuinely public, measurable success, evaluated using the same kinds of metrics already covered in that earlier module, directly demonstrated deep learning's own genuine, practical superiority over prior approaches.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing Why AlexNet Is Genuinely A Pivotal Architecture
This connects back to the modern deep learning era's own genuine origin story. AlexNet, already covered in this topic, is genuinely the architecture most credited with launching that era.

Understanding why ReLU and Dropout, both already covered, became genuinely standard practice is another genuine case where AlexNet's own genuinely successful use of both, already covered, directly explains their genuinely widespread later adoption.
10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates AlexNet's own overall structure in code, contrasting its scale against LeNet's own structure already covered in the previous topic.

code.content:
# A genuinely simplified sketch of AlexNet's own layer sequence, already covered as the overall structure in this topic
alexnet_layers = [
    {"type": "conv", "filters": 96, "filter_size": 11, "activation": "relu"},  # larger early filters, already covered
    {"type": "max_pool", "pool_size": 3},
    {"type": "conv", "filters": 256, "filter_size": 5, "activation": "relu"},
    {"type": "max_pool", "pool_size": 3},
    {"type": "conv", "filters": 384, "filter_size": 3, "activation": "relu"},
    {"type": "conv", "filters": 384, "filter_size": 3, "activation": "relu"},
    {"type": "conv", "filters": 256, "filter_size": 3, "activation": "relu"},
    {"type": "max_pool", "pool_size": 3},
    {"type": "flatten"},
    {"type": "fully_connected", "units": 4096, "dropout": 0.5},  # already covered as popularizing Dropout
    {"type": "fully_connected", "units": 4096, "dropout": 0.5},
    {"type": "fully_connected", "units": 1000},  # 1000 classes, already covered as competition significance
]

lenet_layer_count = 8   # already covered in the previous topic
alexnet_layer_count = len(alexnet_layers)
print(f"LeNet layer count (already covered): {lenet_layer_count}")
print(f"AlexNet layer count: {alexnet_layer_count}")
print(f"AlexNet is roughly {alexnet_layer_count / lenet_layer_count:.1f}x more layers, already covered as the scale leap in this topic")

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: AlexNet is the architecture that helped launch the modern deep learning era.
It is dramatically larger than LeNet, both in depth and parameter count.
Its scale only became practical thanks to Graphics Processing Unit training.
It popularized ReLU over Sigmoid and Tanh, helping address vanishing gradients.
It helped popularize Dropout as a practical, effective regularization technique.
It follows the same convolution-then-fully-connected pattern as LeNet, just at much larger scale.
Its earliest layers use somewhat larger filters, a choice later architectures reconsidered.
It won a major image classification competition by a dramatic margin, demonstrating deep learning's practical superiority.
Next up: VGG, an architecture that explored using consistently small filters stacked much more deeply.
